# Optional statement about the importance of the paper. The heading can be customized in the language field.
impact-statement: "Scientific programming workflows are becoming more complex, 
while existing support mechanisms often remain poorly matched to that complexity. 
We see Quarto Manuals as a practical contribution to this problem and as 
directly aligned with the interests of the US-RSE community. Research software 
engineers are often responsible not only for building software, but also for 
making workflows understandable, reproducible, maintainable, and usable by others. 
Quarto Manuals are designed to support that work by combining explanation, 
code execution, and verification in an ordered, operator-facing format. 

This contribution has three main highlights. First, our work promotes 
technical resources for documenting and delivering rigorous, complex 
scientific workflows. Second, it supports the visibility and value of 
research software engineering by treating workflow design, execution, 
and handoff as first-class engineering artifacts, rather than incidental burdens 
or purely local practice. Third, it serves the broader community by 
making it easier for collaborators with different levels of programming 
experience to run, inspect, and adapt computational workflows in 
a structured and auditable way.

Perhaps most importantly, Quarto Manuals are also intended to 
be complementary to the growing use of AI-assisted programming. As 
AI-generated code becomes more common, research teams will increasingly 
need workflow structures that make human-written instructions _and_ 
LLM-generated code easier to inspect, test, reproduce, and 
maintain together. In that sense, Quarto Manuals may provide 
a useful [harness](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/the-harness-is-all-you-need-mostly/) 
for incorporating AI-assisted programming into scientific workflows, 
without sacrificing rigor or transparency.

Ultimately, we hope Quarto Manuals helps make scientific 
programming more accessible, reproducible, and inclusive, 
while supporting the high standards of software engineering and 
collaboration that the US-RSE community promotes."
